name: @dudo/admin
description: Dudo platform-administration console — React SPA for admin.dudo.work (ADR 0010, 0022, 0024, 0025)

scripts.//verify:kdf MOVED 2026-09-09: The KDF and its suite are `@dudo/client-kdf` (ADR 0040 step 4). This console's copy carried a CROSS-CLIENT DRIFT CHECK comparing kdf.ts's normative region, kdf-client.ts and kdf-worker.ts against platform/web byte for byte — it retired with its subject, because there is one copy now and nothing to compare it to. It was a good check and it had one blind spot that cost real coverage: it covered three files and NOT the file it lived in, which is how the two suites diverged in both directions while the implementations they tested stayed byte-identical.
scripts.//smoke: Loads the BUILT console in a headless browser. THIS FILE EXISTS BECAUSE OF WHAT IT CAUGHT HERE: after the router migration `tsc` exited 0, `vite build` exited 0 and `npm run verify` reported 584 passing assertions — and the console was a blank page. `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'Mn' before initialization`, a circular import route-tree -> root-layout -> AdminShell -> route-tree. A module cycle is legal TypeScript and legal ES and is a property of the IMPORT GRAPH, so no instrument that reads a file can see it; the 33 assertions in verify-platform.mjs that read screen source all passed CORRECTLY on a dead application, because every file they read was fine and the composition was broken. It also caught `redirect()` thrown from a component body, which throws where the router is not listening. ⚠ WHAT A PASS DOES NOT MEAN: this console has NO FIXTURE TRANSPORT by deliberate decision (`a fixture transport is a fake API by another name`), so with no Core running the gate renders its own state and THE ROUTED SECTIONS ARE NOT REACHABLE. A pass proves the router boots, deep links are served by the SPA fallback, an unmatched address falls back to home, and nothing throws. It does NOT prove Organizations, Templates, Operators or the audit feeds render — that needs a live Core and is a deployed check. FOUR STATES: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 NOT RUN (no browser, nothing verified).
scripts.//smoke SHARES ONE DRIVER WITH platform/: `../../web/scripts/lib/browser-harness.mjs`, imported rather than copied. These are two npm packages that do not depend on each other, and duplicating ~200 lines of DevTools plumbing into both would be the divergence ADR 0040 spent a day removing — a pattern this console has already paid for once, when its verify-kdf drift check covered three files and not the file it lived in. If a third consumer appears the driver earns its own package; two does not.
scripts.//smoke BUILDS FIRST, ADDED 2026-09-11 A: The harness refuses to start when `dist/` is MISSING and says so — it has no way to know when `dist/` is merely OLD. Running `npm run smoke` after an edit but before a build serves the previous bundle, and the browser reports on code that is not the code in the tree. It cost four failures that read exactly like real defects: a language control reported absent AFTER it had been made reachable, and the three RTL assertions that depend on it. THE PRECEDING FAILURE OF THE SAME FOUR WAS GENUINE, which is what made the stale run so convincing — the same output twice, once true and once an artifact. `§11a`: a check that examined the wrong thing reports on it confidently. Building first makes staleness impossible rather than something to remember, and it costs about a second.
scripts.//check:suite-parity RETIRED 2026-09-09: Retired with its subject when ADR 0040 unioned the two verify-kdf suites into `@dudo/client-kdf`. The full record of what it caught — 17 gaps, a mislabelled assertion, an exemption that retired itself, and a defect in the checker's own first run — is in `platform/web/package.json`, which is where the script lived. THE SIXTEEN GAPS ON THIS SIDE INCLUDED THE PRINTABLE-ASCII BOUNDARY for `isSubmittableIdentifier`: DEL refused and tilde accepted were asserted on app.dudo.work and not here, for the same function on this console's own sign-in path.
scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm run verify:platform && npm run build && npm run verify:css

//dependencies: EVERY VERSION IS EXACT. No ^, no ~, anywhere in this file.
PINNED 2026-09-09, BEFORE the root gains its `workspaces` key (ADR 0040), and the order
is the point rather than a detail. 0040 first required pinning to land in the SAME change
as the workspaces key, to avoid a window in which hoisting acts on caret ranges. Pinning
FIRST removes that window instead of shrinking it: once these are exact, hoisting cannot
resolve anything new whenever it happens.
IT CHANGES NOTHING THAT RUNS, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. All twelve
packages already resolved to exactly the versions platform/web pins — react 19.2.8,
react-dom 19.2.8, tailwindcss 4.3.3, vite 7.3.6, typescript 5.9.3 and the rest — so every
value below is the version this tree was ALREADY using. Zero of twelve resolved
differently from web.
WHAT IT PREVENTS is narrow and real: a caret range makes this console's resolution a
question of WHEN SOMEBODY LAST INSTALLED. Two hosts that must render one shared primitive
layer cannot have that depend on install order — and under one hoisted tree the two would
be resolving from the same place, where a range and a pin disagree silently.
THE APPROVED SET (user, 2026-09-08) is shadcn/ui, TanStack Router, TanStack Query,
TanStack Table, React Hook Form and Zod. NONE OF THE SIX IS INSTALLED HERE YET. This
console gains them when the shared primitives arrive from @dudo/ui, which is inside that
approval and is stated in 0040 as a real consequence rather than a detail. A seventh
library is a new user approval, not a judgement call (security.md §7).
